evals.prompt: I've attached evals/files/metadata-sl-anc.json, a small slice I exported from our dev server (it's a copy of the Sierra Leone demo, check the system block for the version). I want to paste it into an AI chat to get help reworking the ANC indicators, and then send the same file to an external consultant. Nothing in it should identify a person, the consultant has no business with our sharing setup or the French translations, and facility GPS points shouldn't go out either. Keep it small, but don't break the indicator formulas. Write the cleaned copy to outputs/metadata-shareable.json and tell me what you did and anything I still need to check.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/transform_metadata.py (or reproduces it) with --anonymize --minimize --unshare --delocalize --drop-coordinates and --schemas references/schemas-v41.json (matching system.version 2.41.3, not a default v42). Then handles what --anonymize cannot see: custom attribute values holding a name and phone number (the org unit 'Facility in-charge' and the data element 'Data element steward' on fbfJHSPpUQD), and free text naming people (org unit comment, indicator, legend set and data set descriptions). Removes system.id and instance hrefs, and warns that free text and custom attribute values need manual review on future exports. Output is valid JSON with no planted names/usernames/emails/phones, no sharing or translations, no org unit geometry, while UIDs and the indicator numerator/denominator survive. Warns that users (including admin M5zQapPyTZI) stay as placeholders and must not be imported into another instance, or drops users entirely.
evals.notes: Anonymise/minimise with a file check; traps: version-matched schema, PII in custom attributeValues and free text that --anonymize does not catch.
assertions: outputs/metadata-shareable.json exists and parses as JSON (python -m json.tool succeeds)

Programmatic: none of these strings occur anywhere in the output file: 'Isatu', 'Kargbo', 'ikargbo', 'Sesay', 'John Traore', 'example.org', '+2327600', 'dummy@dhis2.org', 'ikargbo-openid', 'District ANC focal person', '1988-04-17', 'Fatmata', 'Koroma', '076-000-444', 'Aminata', 'Bangura', 'Conteh'

Programmatic: the output has no system.id (the system block is removed or reduced to non-identifying fields such as version) and no instance href: the strings '0b6c6f55-3a4e-4d5c-9b1e-000000000000' and 'your-instance.org' do not occur

Programmatic: the output contains no key named sharing, userAccesses, userGroupAccesses, publicAccess or translations at any depth, and the Ngelehun CHC org unit (DiszpKrYNg8) has no geometry/coordinates
Programmatic: dataElement fbfJHSPpUQD and indicator Uvn6LCg7dVU are still present, and the indicator's numerator is still exactly '#{fbfJHSPpUQD}' and its denominator '#{h0xKKjijTdI}*0.04'
Uses the 2.41 schema (references/schemas-v41.json or the instance's own schemas) for --minimize, derived from system.version 2.41.3, rather than a default/latest schema

Warns the user that free-text fields (descriptions, comments) and custom attribute values are not reliably caught by automatic anonymisation and need manual review on future exports, and says how this file's cases were handled (the 'Facility in-charge' org unit value, the 'Data element steward' value on fbfJHSPpUQD, and the named people in the org unit comment, indicator, legend set and data set descriptions)

Addresses the users in the file: either removes them, or states that they remain as placeholder users (admin UID M5zQapPyTZI included) and must not be imported into another instance because that would rename/disable its admin

evals.prompt: Copying our child-health and ANC config from the old 2.40 server to the new 2.42 staging box went badly. I ran transform_metadata.py --minimize --unshare --delocalize --schemas references/schemas-v40.json --split-dir ./split on the 2.40 export (to keep the payload small), then import_metadata.py --src ./split --passes 2 against staging. I collected every non-OK response into evals/files/import-responses-2.42.json. Staging has no data yet and I can edit its config. Which of these are real problems, what caused each one, and what exactly should I do before re-running? Dataelements shows no error reports at all, so I assume those went in fine?
evals.expected_output: Groups the errors by root cause, judged on the final pass: (1) E4000 shortName on TrackedEntityType nEenWmSyUEp is caused by --minimize with the 2.40 schema (shortName is not owner+persisted there but is required on 2.42); --minimize must not be used for instance transfer, so re-transform with --unshare --delocalize only. (2) The pass-1 programStages E5002 were deferred forward references that pass 2 resolved, so they are not real. (3) E1127 on the 60-option category is a target-side cap: set metadata.categories.max_options in staging's dhis.conf and restart. The categoryCombo E5002 follows from it, and so does (4) the dataElements 409 with status ERROR and zero error reports, which is a whole-batch Hibernate flush crash (the message names DataElement.categoryCombo), not success: the whole batch was lost. (5) The visualization E5002 on indicator Uvn6LCg7dVU persists in pass 2, so the indicator (and its indicatorType) is really missing from the slice. Recommends a pre-import dangling-reference scan.
evals.notes: Import-error analysis across passes; traps: a 409 with zero error reports, E1127 fixed in dhis.conf, and --minimize with a mismatched schema as the cause of E4000.
assertions: Correctness: rejects the user's assumption. The dataElements response (HTTP 409, status ERROR, empty typeReports) is a whole-batch flush crash in which no data elements were imported, not a clean import

Links the dataElements crash to the missing categoryCombo chain (the category rejected by E1127, then the combo rejected by E5002, then DataElement.categoryCombo resolving to nothing), using the response message rather than the (empty) error reports
Says E1127 is a target-side cap fixed in staging's dhis.conf with metadata.categories.max_options (restart required), rather than telling the user to split or trim the 60-option category

Attributes the E4000 'Missing required property shortName' on the tracked entity type to --minimize with the 2.40 schema (a property that schema does not treat as owned/persisted but 2.42 requires) and says not to use --minimize for instance transfer
Classifies the pass-1 programStages E5002 (program IpHINAT79UW) as deferred forward references resolved in pass 2, i.e. not a real problem, judging by the final pass

Identifies the visualization E5002 for indicator Uvn6LCg7dVU as a genuine missing object because it persists in the final pass, and says to add that indicator (with its indicatorType) to the slice or drop the reference
Gives an ordered re-run plan: fix dhis.conf and restart, re-transform without --minimize, then re-import (optionally with --schemas for dependency-ordered single-pass import)

Does not claim that the default category option/category/category combo/COC UIDs differ on every instance. They are fixed (xYerKDKCefk, GLevLNI9wkl, bjDvmb4bfuf, HllvX50cXC0) on databases created on 2.22 or later and can differ only on older databases; advising to check both sides' defaults is fine

Says that a type missing from a collection of non-OK responses (e.g. categoryCombos absent from pass 2) is not proof that it imported successfully, and recommends verifying on staging by object counts/UIDs per type against the source export

evals.prompt: Two broker instances are up on dev-net: agent-sl42 (Sierra Leone demo seed, 2.42) at http://dhis2-agent-sl42:8080 and agent-empty42 (empty 2.42) at http://dhis2-agent-empty42:8080, both admin/district. Please copy every ANC data element and ANC indicator (names starting with 'ANC') from the SL instance to the empty one, together with whatever they need to actually work there. This is the dry run for doing the same between two real servers next month, so do it the way you'd do it for real, then show me proof that it landed.
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/fetch_metadata.py on the source with --types and --filter for the ANC data elements and indicators, then pulls in their dependency closure (categoryCombos, categories, categoryOptions, categoryOptionCombos, indicatorTypes, plus optionSets/legendSets if referenced) and exports with --unshare --delocalize, not --minimize. Excludes users. Imports with scripts/import_metadata.py using --schemas (or --passes 2) and judges the result by the final pass. Migrates COCs rather than regenerating them, or runs categoryOptionComboUpdate afterwards. Verifies on the target with API counts and UIDs that match the source, and confirms the target admin is untouched.
evals.requires: dhis2-instance: Sierra Leone demo 2.42 (source, seed dhis2-db-sierra-leone_v42) + empty 2.42 (target), both via d2-broker
evals.notes: Live end-to-end transfer; traps: dependency closure beyond the name filter, users/admin clobbering, sharing that does not resolve on the target, and not minimizing for transfer.
assertions: Uses the bundled scripts/fetch_metadata.py and scripts/import_metadata.py (or reproduces their per-type, dependency-ordered behaviour) rather than a single hand-rolled POST of a bulk /api/metadata export

The exported slice includes the dependencies the name filter would miss: at least the categoryCombos, categories, categoryOptions and categoryOptionCombos used by the ANC data elements, and the indicatorTypes used by the ANC indicators
Strips sharing (--unshare at export or --skip-sharing on import) and does not use --minimize for the transfer
Does not import users: no users.json is sent (or --exclude users is passed), and the answer names the admin-UID (M5zQapPyTZI) clobbering risk as the reason
Programmatic: on the target, GET /api/dataElements?filter=name:$like:ANC&fields=id&paging=false and the same for /api/indicators return exactly the same UID sets as on the source
Programmatic: for at least one ANC data element, the categoryOptionCombo UIDs of its categoryCombo on the target equal those on the source (COCs migrated, not regenerated with fresh UIDs)
Programmatic: after the run the target still accepts admin/district (GET /api/me returns 200 with username 'admin')
Reports the import result from the final pass's errors (not pass-1 E5002s) and shows the verification output rather than asserting success

evals.prompt: Our dummy-data generator (evals/files/gen_anc_values.py) filled ANC 1st/2nd/3rd visit for all Bo facilities on our 2.41 test box without complaint. Pointed at a 2.43 Sierra Leone demo test instance, every POST now fails with 'Data set detection failed' and nothing is imported. Same admin user, same data elements. Why, and can you fix the script so it works on 2.43 (and still on 2.41)? Only synthetic values, it's a test box.
evals.expected_output: Explains that 2.43's POST /api/dataValueSets requires a data set: with no dataSet in the payload it tries to detect one and fails when the data elements belong to no data set (E8003) or several (E8002); the fix is an explicit top-level dataSet. The data set's period type and org unit assignment are then checked separately (E8021/E8022). 2.40-2.42 accepted values without a data set silently. Rewrites the script to look up the data set(s) containing each data element, with their periodType and organisationUnits, set dataSet on the payload, generate periods matching the data set's period type, and only target org units the data set is assigned to. Sends a valid categoryOptionCombo from each DE's category combo (an omitted COC is stored under default on 2.43.1). Sends a small sample first (dryRun or small N), parses and prints the import status/conflicts, and groups the payload per data set. Does not blame auth or permissions.
evals.notes: Dummy-data generation; trap: the 2.43-only dataValueSets data-set requirement, which the model cannot know from general knowledge.
assertions: Explains that 'Data set detection failed' on 2.43 means the payload names no data set and the data elements map to no data set (E8003) or to more than one (E8002), and that the fix is to send an explicit top-level dataSet in the payload. Period-type matching and org-unit assignment are presented as separate, later checks (E8021/E8022), not as the cause of the detection failure
States that 2.40-2.42 accepted data values with no data set (which is why the script worked on 2.41), i.e. this is a version change, not a bug in their payload shape
Correctness: does not attribute the failure to authentication, user authorities or the admin's org-unit assignment as the primary cause

The rewritten script determines the data set(s) from the API (dataSets containing these data elements, with periodType and organisationUnits) rather than assuming or hard-coding an unverified data set UID
The rewritten script restricts org units to those the chosen data set is assigned to (intersection with the Bo facilities) and generates periods in the data set's periodType

The rewritten script sends an explicit categoryOptionCombo for every value, taken from the data element's own category combo (the data set element's override if set), e.g. the Fixed/Outreach COCs for the ANC visit elements, not the default COC and not omitted. (On 2.43.1 an omitted COC is not rejected: it is stored under the default COC HllvX50cXC0, which is not in these elements' combo, so the values do not appear in the form cells or in disaggregated analytics)
Programmatic: the rewritten script compiles (python -m py_compile succeeds)

The rewritten script does a dry run (dryRun=true or a small first batch) before the full load, and parses the JSON import summary to print its status, imported/updated/ignored counts and any conflicts; printing only raw response text (r.text) does not pass
